QF.id: Concept and Role of Mutual Fund_10

question.text: Under SEBI categorization, a Large Cap equity fund must invest a minimum of what percentage of total assets in equity and equity-related instruments of large cap companies?

answer.text: 80% in large cap companies (1st to 100th by full market capitalization)
65% in large cap companies (1st to 100th by full market capitalization)
80% in large cap companies (1st to 200th by full market capitalization)
75% in large cap companies (1st to 50th by full market capitalization)

explanation.text: The Logic: Per the workbook (page 49), a Large Cap Fund must invest a minimum of 80% of total assets in equity and equity-related instruments of large cap companies, with large cap defined as the 1st to 100th company by full market capitalization. The Trap: The 65% threshold is the separate equity-oriented test used for taxation purposes (page 155) and is not the SEBI large-cap allocation requirement. Option C mixes the correct percentage with the wrong universe (1st-200th includes mid caps). Option D combines a wrong percentage with a wrong universe. Note: Keep the SEBI large-cap allocation rule (80% in top 100) distinct from the 65% equity threshold that determines equity-oriented tax treatment.
